title: Alert on the links the pool is not using

blocks.text: Last night one of the acquirer's two links reconnected at 02:10 and was refused its sign-on until 06:00. For four hours every purchase went over the other link, and nobody was paged: the alert watches the pool's `isConnected()`, and the adaptor's connection counter looked healthy too.

`PoolMonitor` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PoolMonitor.java` is the new alert. It is built with the same space and the same `check-enabled` setting as the pool it watches, and `skipped()` names the links the pool will not send to right now. Finish `inUse`, the one method marked `TODO`. When you're done, the alert names a link exactly when the pool would pass it over, whatever state its connection and sign-on are in. About six lines.
The tests run real QMUXes and a real `MUXPool` in one JVM. They play the adaptor and the sign-on manager by writing to the space.

cases.says: with every link connected and signed on nothing is named, and a link that drops is named
with check-enabled a link that is connected but not signed on is not in use
a sign-on belongs to one connection: after a reconnect the old mark no longer counts
the enabled mark must be the very ready object; an equal copy does not count
without check-enabled a connected link is in use with no sign-on mark at all

origin.section: 14.3 A Link Is Usable When It Is Connected and Signed On

concepts: With check-enabled a member is usable only while its enabled mark is the very ready object of its current connection; without it a connected member is usable.
